title: Organic Chemistry
standard_text: Naming and drawing hydrocarbons (alkanes, alkenes, alkynes, aromatics); functional groups (alcohols, aldehydes, ketones, carboxylic acids, esters, ethers, amines, amides); isomers; addition, substitution, condensation, combustion and polymerization reactions. (summary of The Ontario Curriculum, Grades 11 and 12: Science (2008), Chemistry, Grade 12, University Preparation (SCH4U), Strand B: Organic Chemistry)
meta_desc: Free Grade 12 Chemistry (SCH4U) worksheets on organic chemistry: naming hydrocarbons, functional groups, alcohols, aldehydes, ketones, carboxylic acids, esters, amines, isomers and organic reactions. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: The functional group decides the family and most of the properties.
key_sub: Name from the longest chain; number from the end nearest the functional group.
body_html:
How to think about it

Alkanes (CnH2n+2) have only single bonds, alkenes have a C=C double bond and alkynes a C≡C triple bond. Prefixes give the chain length: meth-, eth-, prop-, but-, pent-, hex-. Number the chain so the double bond or functional group gets the lowest number.

Functional groups: –OH (alcohol, -ol), –CHO (aldehyde, -al), C=O in the chain (ketone, -one), –COOH (carboxylic acid, -oic acid), –COO– (ester, -oate), –NH₂ (amine). Alkenes undergo addition; an alcohol and an acid form an ester and water (condensation); many small monomers join into polymers.

Example

Name CH₃CH₂CH₂OH.

Three carbons: prop-

–OH on carbon 1

Answer: propan-1-ol (1-propanol)

Example

Ethanoic acid + methanol → ?

Acid + alcohol → ester + water

Answer: methyl ethanoate and water

Common mistakes

  • Counting the longest chain wrongly when it bends on the page.
  • Mixing up aldehydes (C=O at the end) and ketones (C=O inside the chain).
  • Naming the ester with the acid part first: the alcohol part comes first (methyl ethanoate).

items.q: Why is benzene less reactive than cyclohexene towards bromine?
c: its delocalized electrons are spread out, so the electron density is lower
items.e: Benzene needs a halogen carrier such as FeBr₃.

items.q: What is the name of the ester made from methanoic acid and butan-1-ol?
items.e: The alcohol part is named first (butyl), then the acid part (methanoate).

items.q: Which test distinguishes an aldehyde from a ketone?
items.e: Ketones are not oxidized by mild oxidants.

items.q: What does 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine (2,4-DNPH) detect?
items.e: Both aldehydes and ketones react.

items.q: Why is phenylamine a weaker base than ethylamine?
c: the nitrogen lone pair is delocalized into the benzene ring
items.e: The lone pair is less available to accept a proton.

items.q: What is formed when an aldehyde is reduced with NaBH₄?
items.e: H⁻ (hydride) attacks the carbonyl carbon.

items.q: Ethyl propanoate is hydrolyzed. Which acid and alcohol form?
items.e: Split at the C–O bond: the -oate part gives the acid, the -yl part gives the alcohol.

items.q: What is used to give a coloured spot for amino acids in chromatography?
items.e: Amino acids are colourless.

items.q: What is a racemic mixture?
c: a mixture of E and Z isomers
equal amounts of two enantiomers, so it does not rotate plane-polarized light
items.e: The rotations cancel.

items.q: What does ethanal form with HCN?
items.e: Nucleophilic addition of CN⁻.

items.q: Which aldehyde undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction?
items.e: Benzaldehyde also does.

items.q: What links the amino acids in a protein?
items.e: Formed by condensation, losing water.

items.q: Methyl propanoate is hydrolyzed. Which acid and alcohol form?
items.e: Split at the C–O bond: the -oate part gives the acid, the -yl part gives the alcohol.

items.q: What is decarboxylation?
c: removal of CO₂ from a carboxylic acid salt, often with soda lime
items.e: Sodium ethanoate gives methane.

items.q: What is the name of the ester made from propanoic acid and pentan-1-ol?

items.q: Which polymer is made by addition polymerization?
items.e: Condensation polymers lose a small molecule as they form.

items.q: What is the zwitterion of an amino acid?
c: an ion with both a positive (NH₃⁺) and a negative (COO⁻) group
items.e: Found at the isoelectric point.

items.q: What is the name of the ester made from pentanoic acid and methanol?
items.e: The alcohol part is named first (methyl), then the acid part (pentanoate).

items.q: Which reagent distinguishes an aldehyde from a ketone?

items.e: Aldehydes are oxidized; ketones are not.

items.q: Which is the strongest base?
items.e: The alkyl group pushes electrons onto the nitrogen lone pair.

items.q: Why do primary amines have higher boiling points than tertiary amines of similar mass?
c: primary amines form hydrogen bonds; tertiary amines cannot
items.e: Tertiary amines have no N–H.

items.q: What is the monomer of poly(propene)?
items.e: Remove “poly” and the brackets to find the monomer.

items.q: How many moles of oxygen are needed to burn one mole of C<sub>16</sub>H<sub>34</sub> completely?
items.e: C<sub>n</sub>H<sub>2n+2</sub> + (3n+1)/2 O<sub>2</sub> → nCO<sub>2</sub> + (n+1)H<sub>2</sub>O. 16 CO₂ need 32 O atoms, 17 H₂O need 17 O atoms: 49 ÷ 2 = 24½.

items.q: What is made when an alcohol is dehydrated with hot concentrated phosphoric acid?
items.e: Water is eliminated.

items.q: Which two compounds react to make propyl ethanoate?
items.e: Propyl- comes from propanol; -ethanoate comes from ethanoic acid.

items.q: Which polymer is used for packaging and disposable cups?
items.e: Poly(phenylethene) (polystyrene): packaging and disposable cups.

items.q: Which ester is made when ethanoic acid reacts with methanol?
items.e: The alcohol gives the first part (methyl) and the acid gives the second part (ethanoate). Water is also made.

items.q: Which two compounds react to make propyl methanoate?
items.e: Propyl- comes from propanol; -methanoate comes from methanoic acid.

items.q: What is the repeating unit of poly(ethene)?
items.e: The C=C opens up to join the monomers.

items.q: Which ester is made when propanoic acid reacts with methanol?

items.q: Which ester is made when methanoic acid reacts with propanol?
items.e: The alcohol gives the first part (propyl) and the acid gives the second part (methanoate). Water is also made.

items.q: Which group shows a +I effect?
items.e: Alkyl groups release electrons.

items.q: Which alcohol forms a carboxylic acid when heated under reflux with excess acidified dichromate?

items.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH<sub>2</sub>BrCH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>3</sub>?

items.q: What is the monomer of poly(ethene)?
items.e: Remove “poly” and the brackets to find the monomer.

items.q: What is the monomer of poly(phenylethene) (polystyrene)?
items.e: Remove “poly” and the brackets to find the monomer.

items.q: Which monomer, tetrafluoroethene, is used to make an addition polymer? Choose its formula.
items.e: Every addition monomer has a C=C double bond.

items.q: In free-radical substitution, which step makes two radicals from one molecule?
items.e: Cl₂ → 2Cl• in UV light.

items.q: Which test shows that a compound is an alkene?
c: bromine water turns from orange to colourless
items.e: Bromine adds across the C=C.
